actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository is a two-armed robot cooking simulation built in MuJoCo
Two 7-DOF arms are driven by the same operational-space impedance controller
The README lists kitchen_scene.xml as the stir stage with two arms, a pot and a spoon
The kitchen scene is the MJCF model 'bimanual_kitchen'
The scene is self-contained: it is built from primitives, needs no external meshes and carries the two 7-DOF arms and a rigidly attached spoon
The scene compiles with the radian angle unit and automatic limits
The scene sets the integration step to 0.002 s with the implicitfast integrator and gravity -9.81 m/s^2
The arm default class gives every arm joint hinge damping 2.0, armature 0.1 and frictionloss 0.2
The nested arm_actuator default class sets each motor's control range to -80 to 80 with gear 1
The right arm has seven hinge joints r_j1 to r_j7 with the ranges -2.9 to 2.9, -1.8 to 1.8, -2.5 to 2.5, -2.9 to 2.9, -2.0 to 2.0, -2.9 to 2.9 and -2.0 to 2.0 rad
The left arm has seven hinge joints l_j1 to l_j7 with the same ranges as the right arm's
The actuator section declares 14 motors, r_m1 to r_m7 and l_m1 to l_m7, one for each arm joint
The stir task loads models/kitchen_scene.xml with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path and creates an MjData
The runner advances the model with mujoco.mj_step
The required Python packages are mujoco 3.0 or newer, numpy, imageio and pillow

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the MJCF deterministically from the reset state and the model has no random element, so one ctrl sequence and tick count repeat the trajectory.  The package's fake backend is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses models/kitchen_scene.xml for the 2 ms step, the 14 qpos and 14 dof hinge coordinates and the 14 motor ctrlranges, then moves each actuated joint toward its control value; it computes no inertias, contacts, friction loss, armature, gravity or actuator dynamics, so no trajectory here is a MuJoCo result
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine
only models/kitchen_scene.xml is served: the clone's pan_flip, pan_pour, bottle, cook and omelette_* scenes (and their free joints and generated props) are not exposed by this package
the scene has no keyframe; reset calls mj_resetData and starts from the model defaults, not from a home pose
no rendering, cameras or sensor publication: the scene has no sensor stream and the bridge exposes only time, qpos, qvel and ctrl
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by the model's 2 ms step only
snapshot and restore use the stand-in integration state; the bridge offers them but the CL3 gate does not exercise them
the scene is a simulation asset: no physical robot or kitchen is modelled or controlled and nothing here was validated against hardware

measures.description: Simulated time since the last reset
measures.name: time_ms

measures.description: Control vector last applied to the actuators (ctrl)
measures.name: ctrl

measures.description: Integration steps since the last reset
measures.name: tick

measures.description: Integration step of the model (null when the model states none)
measures.name: timestep_ms

measures.description: Seed the bridge was configured with
measures.name: seed

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the world state stays readable
